rationale.complete: Round 1 done to the precondition stop: dated predictions; structural count before any freeze time (17 units, 178 readers); synthetic on 5 real skeletons (W0-W3 x 500); Amendment A1; 51 structural estimates rows; period READMEs. Not done: freeze touches, K, anchors, natives N1/N2, W4, a frozen confirm.py.
rationale.faithfulness: The model was not confronted with outcomes. The mapping of kickoff read-out calls is built and checked across regimes; the synthetic shows that read and clock alignment are not identifiable at the real read-delay spread. Scorecard A1 B0 C0 D0 E0 F1 G0 H0 I0.
rationale.usefulness: An operator fact with a number: a day-start kickoff reaches 96% of agents within 2 active min (median about 1 min wall clock), so read-out spread cannot delay a freeze after such kickoffs. Whether a mid-day field freezes agents at their read is open.

one_line: Day-start kickoffs are read at boot by 171/178 agents (96%) within 2 active min, with at most 2 delayed active readers per unit (5 needed), so whether the freeze locks to each agent's read or to the kickoff clock is untestable on exploration data.

models.note: Zero-temperature Potts freeze at the read-out update; precondition failed, no freeze time computed
Asynchronous read-out updates; read and clock alignment coincide for day-start kickoffs

v2.claim: In 17 non-reserved day-start kickoff units (G18-G44), 171/178 kickoff readers (96%) read the kickoff within 2 active min at day boot, with at most 2 delayed active readers per unit, so the read-locked vs clock freeze test is untestable on exploration data
v2.scope: 17 kickoff units, regimes I-III; reserved kickoffs not examined
